title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity, from international collaborations to ambitious commercial ventures. As companies jockey for position, the stakes are high, with funding and strategic partnerships shaping the landscape.

themes.title: International Collaborations Heat Up
themes.body: The upcoming ESA-China SMILE mission aims to shed light on Earth's magnetic shield, showcasing a growing trend of international partnerships in space exploration. Meanwhile, the US-Australian alliance is being touted as a strategic advantage in the ever-competitive space domain.

themes.title: Commercial Ventures on the Rise
themes.body: Virgin Galactic is sticking to its guns, promising to launch commercial services this year, while Cowboy Space's audacious plan for 20,000 orbital data centers raises eyebrows and questions about space congestion. These moves signal a shift towards a more commercialized space economy.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy Continues
themes.body: Chinese satellite maker MinoSpace is eyeing a hefty $736 million IPO, while True Anomaly just secured $190 million in Series C funding, suggesting investors are still keen on space ventures despite economic uncertainties. The Defense-Tech IPO window is showing signs of life, hinting at a potential resurgence in public offerings.

themes.title: Defense and Resilience in Focus
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, underscoring the increasing emphasis on securing space assets. Additionally, Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, reflecting the growing intersection of defense needs and space capabilities.
